key_insight: MemRec introduces a shared, compact collaborative semantic memory for agentic recommender systems, enabling agents to exchange and evolve social/contextual signals without overwhelming their reasoning capacity or incurring high computational cost.
problem_solved: Existing agentic recommenders keep isolated memories and thus miss collaborative signals from user-item graphs; MemRec addresses (a) how to distill large graph contexts into small, useful memory units so agents aren't cognitively overloaded, and (b) how to evolve that collaborative memory efficiently without prohibitive compute.
method: Collaborative memory layer: aggregate multi-agent semantic traces into shared memory entries that capture cross-user and cross-item context.
Graph-to-memory distillation: compress large graph context into sparse, high-utility memory tokens/prototypes to limit per-agent reasoning load.
Efficient evolution mechanism: incremental/low-cost update rules (merge, prune, and lightweight synchronization) to keep the collaborative memory current without expensive retraining.
impact: MemRec enables scalable, socially aware agentic recommenders that leverage collective signals while keeping reasoning and update costs low, making it practical to deploy collaborative memory in production recommender pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: multiple agents interacting with a centralized/shared collaborative memory layer (show read/write paths).
Pipeline flowchart: graph context -> distillation -> compact memory tokens -> agent retrieval and updates.
Bar/stack chart: per-agent cognitive load and compute cost before vs. after MemRec.
Illustrative example: small user-item graph showing how collaborative memory captures cross-user signals (highlighted prototypes).
paper_title: MemRec: Collaborative Memory-Augmented Agentic Recommender System
paper_authors: Weixin Chen, Yuhan Zhao, Jingyuan Huang, Zihe Ye, Clark Mingxuan Ju
